clue.text: Plant drink on account in recession

indicators.note: something in recession goes backwards, so the drink and the account abbreviation are read in reverse order

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer, a drink
A/C is the banking abbreviation for account, as in on account

explanation.surface: Someone buys a plant on credit while the economy is in a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' reverses the whole run of drink plus account, not each piece separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Catmint is a herb whose scent cats adore, a garden plant.

clue.text: Some sacred opinions

definitions.note: the answer is a singular statement of beliefs, standing for opinions held together

indicators.note: some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run hiding within them

explanation.surface: A remark about holding certain religious views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run from saCRED Opinions; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of beliefs or principles, the views a person professes.

clue.text: Port is more flavoursome

definitions.meaning: a Moroccan harbour city on the Strait of Gibraltar
comparative of tangy, sharper in taste

explanation.surface: A harbour town is said to have the stronger taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan seaport has the same spelling as the comparative of tangy, meaning sharper tasting.

clue.text: Unwilling to say after 1.10, perhaps

indicators.note: after places the word for say behind the rearranged figures

parts.note: the figure 1 resembles the letter I

indicators.note: perhaps hints the figure ten is to be taken loosely, its letters rearranged

parts.note: 10 is ten written in figures
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to speak once it is ten past one.
explanation.walkthrough: '1.10' looks like a time; read it as the figures 1 and 10, with 'perhaps' scrambling the ten. 'Unwilling' means without a will, not reluctant.
explanation.definitionFit: A person dying without having made a legal will is in this state, so un-willed is the pun.

clue.text: Try small drink, and chat

parts.note: to have a go is to try
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to sip is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone tastes a little drink and has a natter.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk about others is a synonym for chat or tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Nothing left from relative weight

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing

indicators.note: from signals the letter for left is taken out of the relative

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

explanation.surface: A relation's weight has dropped to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left from' is the removal: the letter for left comes out of the relative, which then follows the zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperial unit of mass, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Buy a bird

definitions.meaning: to buy a story is to believe it, accept it unquestioningly

explanation.surface: An instruction to purchase a feathered creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a tall story credulously is to gulp it down; the migratory songbird has the same name.

clue.text: Write endless abuse on a projection of land

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the abuse word is cut off

parts.note: an insult is verbal abuse

explanation.surface: Someone scrawls graffiti of rude words on a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims INSULT to INSUL; 'on' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of land jutting into the sea, almost an island.

clue.text: Only a few cause an upset

definitions.note: the answer is slang for a trifling sum of money

indicators.note: cause is taken as make, the letters being made into a new word

explanation.surface: Just a handful of people can cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an upset' supplies the seven letters and 'cause' signals they are rearranged; 'upset' tempts as the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a paltry sum, a tiny amount barely worth counting.

clue.text: Weird Scottish king beheaded by the state

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Duncan was a king of Scotland, murdered in Macbeth
NY is the abbreviation for New York State

explanation.surface: Something strange about a Scottish monarch executed by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish' tempts as canny, but the king is Shakespeare's Duncan; 'by' means beside, putting the state after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie or supernatural in a way that is hard to explain, strange.

clue.text: Delicate creature in pain having fluid injected, under the doctor

indicators.note: in a down answer under places the pain word below the doctor

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: injected means put inside, the fluid abbreviation going into the pain word

parts.note: agony is great pain

explanation.surface: A patient in agony is given a drip by the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injected' needs the fluid abbreviation inside the pain word, giving AGONFLY; 'under' sets that below the doctor in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender insect with gauzy wings, frail-looking though a fierce hunter.

clue.text: Hapless Tories rise, so spit

indicators.note: hapless suggests luckless and in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Unlucky Conservatives get up, so someone spits in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hapless' rearranges TORIES RISE; 'spit' looks like a verb but is the roasting rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating skewer for roasting meat, as in a rotisserie oven.

clue.text: Tiger's relative on 21 across, we hear

definitions.note: a fellow member of the cat family; the 's is a link meaning is

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is said aloud

parts.note: the seaside place for playing the game with clubs is called links

explanation.surface: A big cat is found next to a sports ground, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: '21 across' stands for its own answer, a ground for golf, called LINKS by the sea; 'Tiger' may hint at Woods, but it is the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild cat with tufted ears, a smaller cousin of the big striped feline.

clue.text: Old country starts to blossom under rejuvenated ministers, apparently

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of each following word are taken

explanation.surface: A former nation begins to flourish under a renewed government.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of the last five words spell the old name of Myanmar.
explanation.definitionFit: Myanmar's former name, so a nation by a now-superseded title.

clue.text: Hit upon doubly hot river, watery dwelling

indicators.note: in a down answer upon puts the hit word on top of the rest

parts.note: to bat is to hit

indicators.note: doubly means the abbreviation for hot appears twice

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a twice-heated river, a damp home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' gives HH; 'upon' puts BAT above HH + OUSE in the down light. The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A building for bathing, hence a place given over to water.

clue.text: Fag would turn out to be very bad

indicators.note: to turn out is to change shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cigarette would prove to be awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' rearranges FAG WOULD; 'Fag' is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal for terrible or dreadful, extremely poor in quality.

clue.text: Wreck seed box and wreck church property

indicators.note: to wreck something is to ruin its order, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: a crate is a box

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a seed tray and then vandalises a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' scrambles SEED into DESE; the second 'wreck' belongs to the definition, about defiling a sacred place.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate something sacred, as vandals defiling a church do.

clue.text: Operator holds telephone, initially, for fish

indicators.note: holds means the operator word contains another letter

parts.note: a surgeon is one who operates

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A switchboard worker keeps hold of a phone, hoping for a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T from telephone; 'holds' puts it inside SURGEON. 'Operator' looks like a telephonist.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bony-plated fish famous as the source of caviar.

clue.text: Dregs live around university

indicators.note: around means the word for live goes about the university abbreviation

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: The leftover lowlife hang about near the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps RESIDE about U.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over at the bottom, the remains or sediment.

clue.text: Old picture one copies going round and round

indicators.note: the second round means the turned word goes around the letter for one
going round means the copying word turns back on itself

parts.note: to ape is to copy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old photograph is copied over and over in circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns APES into SEPA; 'round' (the second one) then puts SEPA round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownish-toned old photographs are called by the ink-colour name.

clue.text: The best time to be down

parts.note: a plum job or role is the best one
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The finest moment to feel low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like sad, but it is soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft fluffy feathers on a bird, its plumage covering.

clue.text: So hard, protected by ivory, endlessly

indicators.note: protected by means the hard letter is kept inside the trimmed ivory
endlessly means the last letter of the ivory word is dropped

parts.note: an elephant's tusk is made of ivory
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Something hard is guarded by unending ivory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TUSK to TUS; 'protected by' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In this way, therefore: both words mean accordingly.

clue.text: Thrash about and swear taking in a round here?

definitions.text: Thrash about and swear taking in a round here?

indicators.note: about means the thrashing word is turned around

parts.note: to flog is to thrash

indicators.note: taking in means the swearing word contains the round letter

parts.note: to curse is to swear
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A frustrated player flails and swears his way through eighteen holes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a place where golfers flail and swear during a round.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue for eighteen holes, where players complete a round and often flail and curse.

clue.text: Bird's colour, but not tail, containing black

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: containing means the trimmed colour goes around the black abbreviation
not tail means the last letter of the colour is dropped

parts.note: green is a colour
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A bird's colour, missing its end, includes black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not tail' cuts GREEN to GREE; 'containing' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving waterbird with lobed toes, such as the great crested one.

clue.text: Old lover of elegant one embraced

indicators.note: embraced means the elegant bird holds the letter for one

parts.note: the swan is the byword for elegance, an elegant bird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A former sweetheart held an elegant partner close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced' puts I inside SWAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or poetic word for a young male suitor or beau.

clue.text: Like an anagram, I was winning

parts.note: I refers to the setter, whose pseudonym is Mudd
led means was ahead, winning

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being ahead in a word-jumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the setter speaking: this puzzle's compiler is Mudd.
explanation.definitionFit: Anagrams are letters jumbled up, so mixed up or confused.

clue.text: Nutty fruit

explanation.surface: A crazy piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for crazy or mad; also the plural of the curved yellow tropical fruit.

clue.text: Team bringing the Spanish level

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
even means level

explanation.surface: A side brings Spain level in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing' just joins the pieces; 'the Spanish' means the Spanish word for the.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this many players.

clue.text: Flower cut off pole

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A bloom is snipped off a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword joke for a river, something that flows; the Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, a crossword pun on blossom.
